text:
On Monday at 11:55 AM (Bangkok time), Bangchak Corporation Public Company Limited (SET: BCP) gained 2.94% or THB 1.25 to THB 43.75, with a trading value of THB 340.28 million.

Maybank Securities (Thailand) has reiterated its ‘Buy’ recommendation on BCP and raised the target price to THB 61.00 per share from the previous THB 54.00. This upgrade follows an upward revision of the company’s earnings per share estimates by 22-50% for 2026–2029. This is attributed to stronger gross refining margins (GRM), driven by a limited increase in new refining capacity entering the market.

The brokerage has also increased its earnings estimates for BCP’s sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) business, reflecting higher utilisation rates and margin spreads. Meanwhile, the decline in oil prices is not seen to have a material impact, as profits from the exploration and production (E&P) segment are projected to contribute only about 3–6% of the company’s total profits in 2026–2028, despite a seemingly high EBITDA contribution.

Since April, BCP’s share price has risen only 7%, compared to approximately 30% gains for other refinery stocks such as Thai Oil and SPRC, indicating that BCP remains a laggard within the sector. The current valuation is considered attractive, trading at a price-to-book value ratio of 0.6x and a price-to-earnings ratio of 6x based on 2027 data. Maybank expects the company’s strong earnings in 2Q26–3Q26 and the potential revival of a share buyback program to act as short-term catalysts.

On refining margins, Maybank has raised its 2026 Singapore GRM forecast to $12 per barrel from $6, and to $7 / $6 / $6 per barrel for 2027–2029 from $5.5 previously. Refineries continue to be the preferred sub-sector within energy, as global supply remains tight with new refinery capacity averaging just 0.5 million barrels per day for 2026–2028, compared to 1 million barrels per day over the previous three years. Combined with low inventory levels and a delayed increase in global refinery utilisation rates, this should help sustain high GRMs in the near future.

For the SAF segment, Maybank now projects annual EBITDA of THB 3.9 billion due to improved margin spreads and utilisation. Alongside the recently acquired Hong Kong retail oil business, the new channel is expected to generate a combined EBITDA of over THB 5 billion annually, beginning in 3Q26. Notably, the brokerage sees the market as underestimating the earnings growth from the new businesses.

Lastly, the potential impact of lower oil prices has already been factored into Maybank’s forecasts and is not considered a significant downside risk. Although the E&P business accounts for roughly one-third of total EBITDA, its profit contribution is only around 3–6% for 2026–2028 due to high petroleum tax rates and Bangchak’s 45% stake in this unit.

text:
European Commission unveils sweeping carbon market reforms

The European Commission has proposed major reforms to the EU Emissions Trading System (ETS), easing the pace of emissions cuts while increasing financial support for industrial decarbonization.

The proposals would slow the annual decline in carbon permits, extend free allowances for heavy industry until 2038, and allow international carbon credits to meet 2% of ETS emissions reductions from 2036.

The Commission also proposed a €30 billion clean technology investment fund backed by 400 million carbon permits, alongside access to a further €70 billion in allowances from 2031. Governments would be required to spend at least 50% of future ETS revenues on domestic industry.

The reforms would expand the ETS to cover more flights, smaller ships, and waste incineration. The proposals now move to negotiations with EU member states and the European Parliament.

All 27 EU states face infringement proceedings over delays in implementing revised Building Directive

The European Commission has launched infringement proceedings against all 27 EU member states for failing to fully implement the revised Energy Performance of Buildings Directive by the 29 May 2026 deadline.

The directive requires all new buildings to be zero-emission by 2030, with publicly owned buildings meeting the standard from 2028. It also sets a 2040 target to phase out fossil fuel boilers and requires member states to develop national renovation plans.

The Commission said buildings are the “single largest energy consumer in Europe”. It stressed that implementing the EPBD is essential to boosting the annual renovation rate, cutting the EU’s dependence on imported fossil fuels and achieving a fully decarbonized building stock by 2050.

Governments have two months to respond before the Commission can escalate the cases and seek financial penalties through the EU Court of Justice.

Delta and Shell expand sustainable aviation fuel partnership

Delta Air Lines has signed a five-year agreement with Shell Aviation to expand sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) supply and infrastructure across five major US airports.

Under the new agreement, Shell will support SAF deliveries at Los Angeles, Portland, New York JFK, Boston, and Minneapolis-St. Paul. The companies will also build out the logistics and infrastructure needed for wider SAF use in routine airline operations, while exploring next-generation fuels such as alcohol-to-jet and power-to-liquid technologies.

Delta aims for SAF to account for 10% of its fuel use by 2030 as part of its goal to reach net zero emissions by 2050.

Walmart, General Mills, and ADM expand regenerative agriculture partnership

Walmart, General Mills, and ADM have launched a collaboration to expand regenerative agriculture across 40,000 wheat acres in the US Midwest. The program aims to improve soil health, water quality, and carbon sequestration.

The initiative will support farmers in Illinois, Indiana, and Missouri by providing technical assistance and financial incentives to help them adopt regenerative farming practices. ADM will lead implementation, building on its management of nearly 5 million regenerative acres globally.

The partnership expands a 2023 Walmart-General Mills program targeting 600,000 acres by 2030. The companies said more than 560,000 wheat acres are already involved in regenerative agriculture projects.

text:
[수소신문] 지속가능항공유(SAF) 가격이 호르무즈 해협 봉쇄 여파로 큰 폭의 상승세를 보이는 가운데, 향후 1년간 높은 가격 수준이 이어질 것이라는 전망이 나왔다.

석유제품 가격 상승으로 바이오연료 수요가 확대되고 유럽과 미국의 정책 변화가 맞물리면서 SAF 시장의 가격 강세가 지속될 것이라는 분석이다.

블룸버그NEF(BNEF)는 지난 16일 발표한 ‘지속가능항공유(SAF) 가격 전망: 상승세 둔화(Sustainable Aviation Fuel Price Outlook: Leveling Off)’ 보고서를 통해 세계 최대 SAF 소비시장인 북서유럽의 SAF 가격이 향후 1년간 평균 톤당 2746달러를 기록할 것으로 전망했다.

보고서에 따르면 호르무즈 해협 봉쇄 이후 글로벌 연료시장의 불확실성이 확대되면서 2026년 SAF 가격 변동성이 크게 높아졌다. 북서유럽의 2026년 2분기 평균 SAF 가격은 톤당 2830달러(갤런당 8.58달러)로, 2026년 평균 가격보다 31% 상승했다.

같은 기간 북서유럽의 제트연료 평균 가격은 톤당 1404달러를 기록해 SAF 가격은 일반 제트연료의 약 두 배 수준을 유지했다.

BNEF는 석유제품 가격 상승이 도로 운송 부문의 바이오연료 수요를 끌어올리고 있다고 분석했다. 각국 정부가 연료비 부담을 완화하기 위해 바이오연료 사용 확대를 추진하면서 SAF를 비롯한 재생연료 시장에도 영향을 미치고 있다는 설명이다.

유럽에서는 정책 변화도 시장에 영향을 주고 있다. 일부 유럽연합(EU) 회원국은 재생에너지지침 III(RED III)을 자국 법령으로 이행하는 과정에서 첨단 바이오연료에 적용하던 '이중 산정(Double Counting)' 제도를 폐지했다.

이에 따라 수첨식물성오일(HVO) 수요가 증가하면서 유럽 생산업체들은 HVO 생산을 확대하는 한편 미국과 아시아·태평양 지역으로부터 SAF 수입도 늘릴 것으로 전망됐다.

미국에서는 바이오매스 기반 디젤의 혼합 의무제도가 최종 확정되면서 원료 가격이 상승하고 있다. 이에 따라 미국의 SAF 생산비는 빠르게 오르고 있으며, 2026년 5월 기준 아시아·태평양과 유럽보다 톤당 약 1000달러 높은 수준을 기록한 것으로 나타났다.

아시아에서는 중국이 2025년 아시아 최대 재생연료 생산국으로 부상했다. 2026년 1분기에는 SAF 가격 약세의 영향으로 수출이 둔화됐지만, 가격이 상승한 4월 이후에는 수출이 다시 회복세를 보이고 있다.

BNEF는 현재 대부분의 SAF가 장기 구매계약(Offtake Agreement)을 통해 거래되고 있어 공개 가격 정보가 제한적이며 시장 전망도 쉽지 않다고 설명했다.

이에 실거래 가격 데이터와 손익분기 생산비(Breakeven Cost), 시장 수급 여건 등을 종합적으로 반영해 북서유럽과 미국 걸프코스트, 싱가포르 시장의 SAF 선도가격(Forward Curve)을 모델링하고 있다고 밝혔다.

title: Lufthansa stock trades steady as traffic recovery meets cost pressures

text:
Lufthansa Group (ISIN DE0008232125), the German airline group listed in Frankfurt, saw its Lufthansa stock mirror the mixed picture in the aviation sector, with improving traffic and revenue contrasted by lingering cost and competitive pressures. In its 2023 annual results, Lufthansa reported a notable increase in revenue compared with the prior year, while profitability and margins remained sensitive to fuel costs, labor expenses, and fleet modernization commitments. For investors, the current setup combines cyclical tailwinds from travel demand with strategic and financial discipline requirements to sustain earnings.

Revenue up versus prior year

According to the Lufthansa Group annual report for 2023, the company generated revenue of around EUR 35 billion for the year, up clearly from approximately EUR 32 billion in 2022, underscoring the ongoing recovery in passenger and cargo demand following the pandemic-related slump. This increase reflects higher load factors, improved yields in key European and intercontinental markets, and the contribution from premium brands in the group airline portfolio. The revenue growth of roughly EUR 3 billion year on year provided a base for better operating leverage, even as the company continued to absorb higher input costs.

In the same 2023 period, Lufthansa reported an adjusted EBIT—a key profitability metric watched by the market—that returned to a solid positive level after the severe downturn in earlier crisis years. The move from low or negative EBIT during the pandemic to positive, multi-billion euro adjusted EBIT in 2023 marked a turning point in the financial trajectory. The improvement was driven by capacity restoration, network optimization and cost measures, yet margin percentages remained below pre-crisis peaks, signaling that the recovery phase was not yet complete and that additional efficiency gains would be needed.

Passenger volumes and earnings comparison

Lufthansa’s operational data for 2023 also showed a clear rise in passenger numbers compared with 2022, as both leisure and corporate travel demand strengthened. The group carried many tens of millions of passengers in 2023, significantly above the prior year’s tally, and capacity measured in available seat kilometers approached levels seen before the pandemic. This increase in traffic not only supported revenue but also helped dilute fixed cost burdens across a larger base of flights, contributing to the turnaround in earnings.

Net income returned to positive territory on a full-year basis in 2023, contrasting sharply with the heavy losses booked in 2020 and 2021 during the peak of travel restrictions and lockdowns. While the absolute net profit was still below pre-2019 highs, the swing from deep losses to profits amounted to several billion euros, which materially strengthened the group’s balance sheet and reduced dependence on state support structures. The comparison with prior loss-making years highlights how sensitive Lufthansa’s bottom line is to capacity utilization and pricing power: relatively moderate shifts in traffic and yield can translate into large changes in net income due to the capital-intensive nature of airline operations.

Cash flow metrics also showed improvement. Operating cash flow in 2023 benefited from higher ticket sales and better working-capital trends, enabling Lufthansa to fund part of its fleet investment program from internal resources. Free cash flow turned positive when compared with the negative levels recorded during the crisis, even after accounting for spending on new aircraft and modernization. This shift in cash generation capacity allowed the group to reduce net debt and interest burdens gradually, which, in turn, supported credit quality and financial flexibility.

Cost structure and margin discipline

The recovery in profitability in 2023 came despite a challenging cost backdrop. Fuel costs remained elevated compared with the pre-pandemic era, driven by energy-market volatility and geopolitical factors, which directly affected Lufthansa’s operating expenses. Labor costs also increased, reflecting collective agreements, wage adjustments and the need to retain and recruit skilled personnel such as pilots, cabin crew and ground staff in a tight labor market. As a result, unit cost management stayed at the center of the group’s strategy, as even modest cost overruns can erode margins in a competitive airline environment.

Lufthansa’s reported operating margin in 2023 improved versus the deeply negative margin levels in 2020 and 2021, yet it did not fully match the best years before the crisis. The margin expansion—from negative territory in pandemic years to positive single-digit or low double-digit range in 2023—illustrated the progress in restoring profitability but also showed that the group still has work to do to reach earlier peak performance. Compared with prior periods, the incremental margin gains were driven more by demand recovery and improved yields than by structural cost reductions, which means that maintaining margins will require vigilance if macroeconomic or demand conditions soften.

On the balance sheet side, Lufthansa reduced net debt in 2023 compared with 2022, aided by positive free cash flow and equity support measures implemented in earlier years. The ratio of net debt to EBITDA improved, signaling reduced financial risk relative to the crisis period when leverage had climbed sharply. This decline in leverage helps lower interest expenses over time and increases resilience against potential shocks, such as fuel-price spikes or demand dips, though the group still carries substantial financial obligations due to its large fleet and infrastructure requirements.

Fleet renewal and investment commitments

Lufthansa’s 2023 and ongoing planning includes significant investment in newer, more fuel-efficient aircraft, supporting both cost and sustainability goals. Orders and deliveries for modern wide-body and single-aisle jets aim to reduce per-seat fuel consumption and maintenance costs compared with older aircraft, which has a direct effect on unit economics and long-term competitiveness. However, these fleet investments also require substantial capital expenditure, running into the billions of euros over the multi-year horizon, and therefore must be balanced against cash-generation capacity and debt targets.

The group’s capital expenditure for 2023 increased versus 2022, reflecting the ramp-up in fleet and product investments. While this higher capex temporarily weighs on free cash flow, management expects the newer aircraft to contribute to improved margins through lower operating costs and potentially higher customer satisfaction, which can support yields. For investors evaluating Lufthansa stock, this trade-off between current cash outflows and future operating benefits is a key strategic consideration: too rapid an expansion or renewal could strain finances, but underinvestment could leave the fleet at a competitive disadvantage.

Segment performance and premium brands

Lufthansa Group’s portfolio includes the core Lufthansa passenger airline along with other brands such as SWISS, Austrian Airlines, Brussels Airlines and Eurowings, each contributing to the group’s overall revenue and earnings. In 2023, premium carriers in the group played an important role in restoring profitability, as business and long-haul leisure travel recovered and premium cabins saw higher occupancy and yields. Revenue per available seat kilometer improved in several premium segments compared with 2022, which helped offset cost pressures.

At the same time, point-to-point and lower-cost operations through brands like Eurowings addressed price-sensitive traveler segments, providing complementary network coverage. The balance between premium and value-focused brands enables Lufthansa to adapt to demand shifts across regions and customer groups. Segment reporting in the 2023 annual accounts showed that some units achieved stronger margin improvement than others, with premium hubs benefiting more from corporate travel recovery, while point-to-point operations faced intense competition from other European low-cost carriers, affecting yield dynamics.

Cargo business and diversification

Lufthansa’s cargo division, which was a major earnings contributor during the peak pandemic years when passenger traffic was depressed, experienced normalization in 2023 as airfreight markets cooled from their earlier highs. Cargo revenue in 2023 declined compared with 2022 as freight rates and volumes adjusted, reducing the extraordinary profit contribution that cargo had provided during the crisis. Nevertheless, cargo operations remained an important diversification element, ensuring that Lufthansa’s earnings do not rely solely on passenger travel cycles.

The decline in cargo revenue compared with the prior year illustrated how quickly market conditions can change in logistics and freight once supply chains stabilize and capacity returns. For Lufthansa, this meant that the group had to rely more on passenger-business recovery to sustain overall growth, increasing the importance of the commercial strategy for passenger markets. The quantified shift—from elevated cargo earnings in 2022 to more normalized levels in 2023—fed directly into the group’s overall revenue mix and margin profile.

Liquidity, state support exit and shareholder structure

During the crisis years, Lufthansa received state-backed support and financing that were critical for its survival. By 2023, the group had largely exited these extraordinary support mechanisms, repaying state loans and redeeming equity-related instruments tied to rescue packages. This exit from state support compared with earlier years signaled restored financial independence and market-based financing, which many investors view favorably as it simplifies the capital structure and reduces political constraints.

Lufthansa’s liquidity levels in 2023 remained robust compared with minimum requirements, with cash and cash equivalents plus available credit lines covering near-term obligations and providing a buffer against volatility. The ratio of liquidity to monthly operating costs improved versus the worst crisis periods, when the group had to manage cash very tightly to avoid shortfalls. This enhanced liquidity position supports stability for Lufthansa stock, as it reduces the probability of sudden financial distress arising from unexpected shocks.

Guidance and outlook metrics

In its forward-looking commentary around the time of the 2023 annual report, Lufthansa provided guidance ranges for capacity, revenue and profitability for the 2024 period, indicating planned capacity expansion and expectations of continued demand recovery. The guidance suggested that available seat kilometers would rise versus 2023, moving closer to or above pre-crisis levels, and projected that revenue and adjusted EBIT in 2024 would at least match or exceed 2023 levels, assuming stable macroeconomic and demand conditions. These quantified outlook metrics, while subject to uncertainty, signaled management’s confidence in sustaining the recovery.

Comparing the guidance for 2024 against actual 2023 performance helps investors assess the implied growth and risk profile. A projected increase in capacity and revenue implies that Lufthansa will be more exposed to demand fluctuations, but also that it can leverage fixed costs over a larger operating base. At the same time, management highlighted risks such as fuel-price volatility, geopolitical tensions, and potential economic slowdowns that could affect travel demand and yields, underscoring that the path from recovery to stable profitability is not linear.

Dividend considerations and capital allocation

Lufthansa’s capital allocation decisions, including the potential resumption or adjustment of dividend payments, are closely tied to its earnings and balance-sheet strength. In prior years marked by losses and crisis conditions, dividend distributions were halted or reduced to preserve cash. With the return to profitability in 2023 and reduced net debt, the company reopened discussions on shareholder returns, evaluating whether the improved financial position justified renewed payouts while maintaining sufficient investment capacity and resilience.

Any dividend policy for 2024 and beyond, when compared with the absence or minimal dividends during the crisis years, would reflect a qualitative and quantitative shift in Lufthansa’s financial health. The magnitude of potential distributions would depend on net income, free cash flow and leverage metrics, with regulators, creditors and rating agencies paying close attention to ensure that payouts do not compromise financial stability. For Lufthansa stock, the possibility of resumed dividends adds another dimension to the investment case beyond pure capital gains and earnings recovery.

Competitive landscape and market share

Lufthansa operates in a highly competitive European and global airline market, where market share and pricing power are influenced by route networks, alliances and service quality. In 2023, the group maintained significant market positions in its core hubs such as Frankfurt and Munich, with home-market shares in certain segments remaining strong compared with rivals. Market-share data for key routes showed Lufthansa holding substantial portions of traffic, particularly in business travel corridors and transatlantic routes, although competition from other network carriers and low-cost airlines remained intense.

Compared with pre-pandemic years, the competitive dynamics have shifted, as some rivals have adjusted capacity or business models, and customer preferences have evolved. Lufthansa’s ability to defend or grow market share in profitable segments is closely linked to its product offering, reliability, and network coordination with alliance partners. Incremental changes in market share, even by a few percentage points on key routes, can materially affect revenue and margin outcomes, reinforcing the importance of strategic route planning and customer experience improvements.

Operational reliability and customer metrics

Operational reliability, including on-time performance and cancellation rates, is a crucial factor in customer satisfaction and brand perception. In 2023, Lufthansa worked to stabilize operations after disruption-heavy years, aiming to reduce cancellations and delays compared with 2022. Internal metrics indicated improvements in punctuality and a reduction in irregular operations, though performance was not uniformly optimal across all hubs and seasons. Better reliability helps protect yields and brand loyalty, thereby supporting long-term revenue and earnings.

Customer metrics such as net promoter scores, satisfaction ratings, and loyalty-program participation also play a role in gauging the strength of Lufthansa’s franchise. In 2023, loyalty-program membership figures and engagement data suggested that customers were returning and again accumulating miles at higher rates than during the pandemic years. Growth in loyalty engagement compared with 2022 levels supports premium-revenue potential, as frequent flyers often generate higher yields and contribute to ancillary revenue streams such as upgrades, lounge access and co-branded credit cards.

Sustainability targets and emissions metrics

Lufthansa has committed to sustainability targets that include reducing CO2 emissions and improving fuel efficiency across its fleet. The group reports metrics such as emissions per passenger kilometer and total CO2 output, providing comparisons between 2023 and prior years. Progress in reducing emissions intensity resulted from both technical improvements in newer aircraft and operational measures like optimized flight planning and load management. While total emissions can rise with increased traffic, improvements in per-unit emissions are key indicators of sustainability progress.

In 2023, Lufthansa’s emissions intensity metrics showed better values compared with earlier years with older fleet compositions, indirectly supporting competitiveness as regulatory and customer scrutiny on environmental performance increases. The company also participates in offset schemes and sustainable aviation fuel initiatives, which can be quantified in terms of volumes used or contracts signed, though these still represent a small fraction of total fuel consumption. For Lufthansa stock, the ability to demonstrate tangible sustainability progress is relevant, as ESG considerations increasingly inform capital allocation decisions for many institutional investors.

Digitalization and ancillary revenue

Digitalization plays a growing role in Lufthansa’s operational and commercial strategy, with initiatives ranging from dynamic pricing to self-service customer interfaces and operational analytics. Digital tools contribute to optimizing load factors, pricing, and route planning, which can yield measurable financial benefits. Ancillary revenue streams such as seat reservations, baggage fees, onboard services and partnerships also generate quantifiable contributions to total revenue, and in 2023, ancillary revenue per passenger increased compared with 2022, reflecting greater adoption of optional services.

The growth in ancillary revenue per passenger helps diversify income beyond base ticket prices, which are subject to intense competition and cyclical swings. By increasing ancillary revenue and improving digital efficiency, Lufthansa aims to lift overall revenue per passenger and margin resilience, even when average fares face pressure. Over time, comparisons of ancillary revenue metrics across years provide insight into how successful the company is in monetizing its customer base more broadly than through traditional ticket sales alone.

Labor relations and cost implications

Labor relations, including negotiations with pilot, cabin crew and ground staff unions, have direct implications for Lufthansa’s cost base and operational stability. Collective bargaining agreements often result in negotiated wage increases and changes to working conditions, which can be quantified in terms of percentage pay rises or cost-impact estimates. In recent periods around 2023, negotiated settlements included multi-year wage adjustments that increased personnel expenses compared with prior contracts, contributing to the overall cost inflation faced by the group.

The balance between fair compensation and cost control is delicate. Wage increases measured in mid-single-digit percentages per annum can add significant costs when applied across tens of thousands of employees. Comparing personnel-cost growth rates to revenue growth provides insight into whether labor expenses are growing in line with or outpacing income. For Lufthansa, ensuring that productivity gains and improved revenue per employee keep pace with higher wages is critical to maintaining margins and avoiding renewed earnings pressure.

Macro environment and demand sensitivity

Lufthansa’s performance is influenced by macroeconomic factors such as GDP growth, business sentiment, consumer confidence and currency movements. In 2023, the macro backdrop was characterized by moderate growth and high inflation in many markets, which affected both demand and costs. Demand for air travel proved resilient compared with initial fears of a sharp slowdown, supporting Lufthansa’s revenue growth, but inflationary pressures on fuel, labor and other inputs compressed margins.

Historically, Lufthansa’s passenger volumes and yields have been sensitive to economic cycles, with recessions or major crises leading to declines in traffic and pricing power, while expansions support growth. Comparing traffic and revenue metrics across different macro phases illustrates this sensitivity. For investors, tracking macro indicators alongside Lufthansa’s own guidance helps anticipate potential shifts in performance: for example, if leading indicators point to slower growth, capacity and cost adjustments may be necessary to protect profitability.

Risk management and hedging strategies

Lufthansa employs risk-management tools such as fuel hedging, currency hedging and insurance to mitigate some of the volatility inherent in airline operations. Fuel hedging volumes and hedge ratios can be expressed numerically, showing what portion of expected consumption is hedged and at what average price level. In 2023, hedging strategies partially cushioned the impact of fuel-price swings compared with unhedged exposure, though hedging is not perfect and carries its own risks if market movements diverge from expectations.

Currency hedging also plays a role, as Lufthansa earns revenue and incurs costs in multiple currencies. The degree of hedging and mismatch between currency inflows and outflows influences reported results when exchange rates move. Quantitative data on hedging positions helps investors understand how much of the group’s earnings volatility is likely due to market movements versus operational performance. Over time, comparisons of hedge effectiveness can reveal whether risk-management strategies have added or detracted value.

Passenger brand and product focus

Lufthansa’s core passenger product centers on network connectivity, premium cabins and service elements such as lounges and digital services. The group invests in cabin refurbishments, seating products and customer-experience upgrades that aim to enhance the perceived value of its offering, allowing for stronger yields on key routes. Quantitatively, investment in product enhancements can be expressed in capital-expenditure budgets dedicated to interiors and service innovations, and in metrics such as premium-cabin load factors or revenue shares.

These product-related metrics, when compared year on year, show whether investments are translating into improved revenue and customer satisfaction. For instance, higher premium-cabin load factors and average fares in 2023 compared with 2022 would indicate that cabin and service upgrades are resonating with customers and generating a financial return. Conversely, if product investments do not yield measurable improvements in revenue per passenger or satisfaction indicators, strategic adjustments may be required to optimize capital allocation.

Lufthansa stock and market value

Lufthansa stock is traded on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, where its price reflects market expectations for the group’s earnings, balance-sheet strength and strategic positioning. text:
Jakarta, SAWIT INDONESIA – Dewan Energi Dubai (Dubai Supreme Council of Energy) menjajaki peluang memproduksi bahan bakar penerbangan berkelanjutan (sustainable aviation fuel/SAF) dari limbah organik yang dihasilkan dari negara tersebut. Dikutip dari Zawya pada Senin (20/7/2026), rencana tersebut dibahas dalam pertemuan Dewan Energi Dubai sebagai bagian dari upaya mendukung transisi menuju sektor penerbangan yang lebih ramah lingkungan.

Inisiatif itu sejalan dengan upaya global untuk meningkatkan porsi penggunaan SAF yang dicampurkan dengan bahan bakar pesawat konvensional dalam beberapa tahun mendatang. Selain menyediakan alternatif bahan bakar yang lebih bersih bagi industri penerbangan, proyek tersebut juga diharapkan memperkuat penerapan ekonomi sirkular di Dubai melalui pemanfaatan limbah organik.

Di dalam negeri, pengembangan SAF juga terus dilakukan salah satunya oleh PT Pertamina (Persero). Perusahaan migas terbesar milik negara itu menggandeng Boeing menandatangani Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) untuk menjajaki pengembangan ekosistem Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) di Indonesia. Ini bagian dari upaya mendukung dekarbonisasi sektor penerbangan dan percepatan transisi energi menuju Net Zero Emission (NZE).

Sejalan dengan visi Asta Cita Presiden Prabowo Subianto, Indonesia terus mendorong pengembangan SAF, salah satu solusi mengurangi emisi karbon di sektor penerbangan sekaligus mendukung terciptanya industri penerbangan yang lebih berkelanjutan.

Berdasarkan laporan ASEAN 2050 SAF Outlook, Indonesia menempati peringkat tiga besar di ASEAN dengan potensi surplus produksi SAF terbesar yang diproyeksikan mencapai 2,2 juta barel per hari pada 2050.

Melalui kerja sama ini, Pertamina dan Boeing akan berkolaborasi dalam menjajaki berbagai aspek pengembangan ekosistem SAF di Indonesia. Termasuk identifikasi potensi bahan baku (feedstock), pengembangan teknologi, serta dukungan terhadap pengembangan kebijakan yang diperlukan guna mempercepat implementasinya.

Direktur Utama PT Pertamina (Persero), Simon Aloysius Mantiri, mengatakan, bagi Pertamina, kolaborasi ini bukan sekadar pengembangan bahan bakar, tetapi investasi jangka panjang untuk membangun ekosistem industri SAF nasional.

text:
Hazer Group Limited (ASX: HZR), an Australian clean hydrogen technology company, has completed a comprehensive Process Design Package with engineering giant Kellogg Brown & Root (KBR) for a 30,000 tonnes per annum hydrogen facility. The milestone represents a significant advancement toward commercial deployment and has triggered increased engagement from potential customers and strategic partners across steel, ammonia, clean fuels and industrial sectors globally. Managing Director Glenn Corrie indicated the company is transitioning from technology development toward commercial execution, with South Australia emerging as a strategically important region for deployment.

Key Points

Hazer Group Limited (ASX: HZR) is an Australian clean hydrogen technology developer focused on producing low-emissions hydrogen and graphite co-products for industrial decarbonisation.

The company completed a comprehensive Process Design Package with KBR for a 30,000 tonne per annum hydrogen facility, a fundamental engineering milestone required to guide project development phases.

Commercial pipeline continues to expand with opportunities being pursued across steel, ammonia, sustainable aviation fuel and renewable diesel sectors in Australia, Asia, the Middle East and Canada.

Hazer maintains a robust $13.0 million funding position with low operating cash burn, and has achieved a patent grant from the Japanese Patent Office strengthening intellectual property protection in a strategic market.

The FortisBC project in Canada advances with KBR engaged on site-specific engineering for a 2,500 tonne per annum proposed commercial facility.

Completion of Hazer-KBR Process Design Package Marks Transition from Development to Commercial Readiness

Hazer Group and Kellogg Brown & Root announced completion of a comprehensive Process Design Package (PDP) for a 30,000 tonnes per annum hydrogen Hazer facility during the quarter ended 30 June 2026. The company stated that this represents a significant advancement in the maturity and commercial readiness of the Hazer Process. The collaborative effort strengthened the Hazer-KBR Alliance by leveraging KBR's global engineering expertise to enhance the credibility, scalability and transferability of the Hazer technology in alignment with the expectations of large international industrial clients.

The PDP serves as a fundamental input into engineering design of major projects and is required to guide initial phases of project development. According to the company update, a customised version of the PDP is developed for each plant, first at the Pre-Front End Engineering & Design (FEED) level, then through FEED to provide guidance for Final Investment Decision (FID) and Post-FID detailed engineering during the execution phase. By completing the PDP process internally with KBR, Hazer stated it significantly reduces the risk of material changes to the process and associated capital and operating expenditure when completing customised customer plant development. The template PDP allows Hazer to optimise process design and conduct evaluations into production throughput, process safety and operations ahead of deploying these to clients.

Hazer's Proprietary Reactor Technology Validated Through Extensive PSRI Testing Program

Hazer's competitive positioning is underpinned by proprietary process equipment, particularly the Hazer reactor design, which has undergone an extensive testing program with Particulate Solid Research, Inc. (PSRI) and substantial model development. The company stated that the combination of the completed PDP covering overall plant design and the proprietary reactor strengthens confidence in Hazer's commercial scale-up methodology. The increased level of engineering rigour and validation achieved during the period further confirms confidence in process performance and reinforces the commercial readiness of the Hazer Process.

This validation framework is designed to support engagement with prospective industrial customers and project partners. Hazer indicated that the comprehensive engineering work completed during the quarter positions the company to progress toward customer-specific plant development with greater certainty regarding process performance and capital requirements. The rigorous testing and modelling approach reduces technical risk for potential customers evaluating deployment of Hazer technology at commercial scale.

Expanding Commercial Opportunities Across Steel, Ammonia, Clean Fuels and Industrial Sectors

Hazer reported that since completion of the PDP, the company has observed increasing commercial engagement across a number of key target markets and geographies, with both Hazer and KBR's business development activities gaining momentum. The company stated that the scale of demand for Hazer's technology continues to grow, underpinned by the capacity selected for the Hazer-KBR Process Design Package and supporting Hazer's scale-up strategy. The commercial pipeline continues to expand, with Hazer and KBR progressing multiple project opportunities across steel, ammonia, clean fuels and industrial sectors.

The macro trend toward energy and fuel security is driving increasing interest for application of Hazer's technology in manufacturing of liquid low emissions fuels including sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and biodiesel, with active opportunities being pursued across Australia, the Middle East and Asia. The green iron and steel market segment continues to present significant growth opportunities with strong interest in large-scale deployment across Australia, Asia (particularly Japan and Korea) and increasingly in the Middle East. Interest is underpinned by Hazer's structural cost advantage in producing low-emissions hydrogen, especially in comparison to electrolysers, combined with the additional value created through its graphite co-product. The company noted that several strategically important commercial opportunities were advancing during the quarter with meaningful progress achieved across key projects and markets, although some larger opportunities with major counterparties remain commercially sensitive.

FortisBC Canadian Project Progresses Toward 2,500 Tonne Per Annum Commercial Facility

The FortisBC project in Canada continues to advance with strong partner engagement. Following successful pilot-scale reactor validation, development work is now focused on defining the process design basis for a 2,500 tonne per annum commercial facility. Development activities are focused on assessing site-specific requirements and evaluating pathways for progression of the engineering program. FortisBC has expanded its engagement with Hazer, strengthened by KBR, on further process design and development activities across a broader range of project scenarios.

Engagement with FortisBC on the commercial framework is ongoing, supporting continued advancement toward a potential first-of-a-kind deployment in Canada. The company did not disclose a timeline for reaching final investment decision or commencement of construction. The Canadian opportunity demonstrates the geographic reach of Hazer's commercial pipeline and the viability of the technology in North American industrial markets.

South Australia Emerging as Strategic Region for Hazer Hydrogen and Graphite Deployment

Managing Director Glenn Corrie highlighted that South Australia is emerging as an increasingly strategic region for Hazer. The progression of M Resources' bid for the Whyalla Steelworks, together with Hazer's collaboration with Hallett Group, demonstrates the potential for Hazer to play a meaningful role in the state's industrial decarbonisation ambitions while advancing multiple pathways to commercialise both Hazer hydrogen and graphite. This regional focus aligns with Australia's broader objectives around manufacturing competitiveness and emissions reduction.

The South Australian opportunity reflects convergence of several factors: proximity to existing steel manufacturing infrastructure, policy support for industrial decarbonisation, and strategic partnerships with established industrial companies. The Hallett collaboration is advancing Hazer's graphite monetisation strategy, driven by the Hallett agreement and successful completion of the graphite pelletisation program. The company stated that Hazer Graphite monetisation progresses through these initiatives, positioning the graphite co-product as an additional revenue stream alongside hydrogen sales.

Market Entry into Renewable Diesel and Sustainable Aviation Fuel Sector via CRV Partnership

Hazer entered the renewable diesel and sustainable aviation fuel market during the quarter through a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with Continuous Renewable Ventures (CRV). This market entry expands the addressable customer base for Hazer's hydrogen production technology beyond traditional industrial hydrogen consumers. The renewable diesel and SAF sectors represent high-growth markets driven by regulatory mandates and corporate sustainability commitments globally.

The CRV partnership opens pathways for Hazer to supply low-emissions hydrogen for production of sustainable fuels, addressing macro trends toward energy security and decarbonisation of the transport sector. The company did not disclose specific commercial terms, project locations, or timelines for the CRV collaboration in this update.

Japanese Patent Grant Strengthens Intellectual Property Protection in Strategic Market

Hazer secured a key patent grant from the Japanese Patent Office during the quarter, strengthening intellectual property protection in a strategic market. Japan represents a significant opportunity for Hazer's technology given the country's industrial decarbonisation ambitions, particularly in the steel and ammonia sectors. The company highlighted strong interest in large-scale deployment in Japan as part of its broader Asia-Pacific strategy.

Intellectual property protection is critical for Hazer's commercialisation strategy as it builds customer confidence and creates barriers to competition. The Japanese patent grant indicates that Hazer's proprietary technology meets patentability standards in a major industrial economy, supporting the company's ability to license or deploy technology in that market. The company did not disclose the specific scope or claims of the patent granted.

Robust Financial Position with $13.0 Million Funding Supporting Low-Burn Operating Model

Hazer reported a robust $13.0 million funding position as of 30 June 2026, reflecting low operating cash burn and prudent financial stewardship through FY26. This funding level is designed to support the company's transition toward commercial execution while maintaining financial flexibility to pursue strategic opportunities. The company did not disclose specific operating cash burn figures or anticipated cash runway in this update.

The strong funding position underpins Hazer's ability to fund engineering work with KBR, progress multiple commercial opportunities, and pursue strategic partnerships without immediate requirement for capital raising. As the company transitions from technology development toward commercial deployment, capital efficiency and disciplined cash management remain important given the capital-intensive nature of hydrogen production facility development and deployment.

Management Webinar Scheduled to Discuss Commercial Progress and Strategic Outlook

CEO Glenn Corrie and other members of the management team will host a webinar on Wednesday, 22 July 2026 at 9:00am (AWST) / 11:00am (AEST) to discuss the company's commercial progress and strategic outlook. This investor communication follows completion of the quarterly activities and cashflow report. The company indicated that registration details and a link to the webinar would be provided separately.

Corrie stated in the company update that Hazer has experienced increased engagement from potential customers and strategic partners pursuing large-scale, low-emissions industrial projects since PDP completion. While increased commercial activity does not always translate into immediate announcements, Corrie noted that the quality and scale of opportunities continue to strengthen, reflecting growing demand for Hazer's secure, scalable and cost-competitive low-emissions hydrogen solution across multiple sectors and geographies. The company indicated it is well positioned to deliver material commercial value as it transitions from technology development toward commercial execution.

Technology Differentiation and Cost Competitiveness Position Hazer in Expanding Decarbonisation Market

Hazer's competitive positioning is underpinned by a differentiated low-cost decarbonisation process that produces both hydrogen and graphite as co-products. The company highlighted its structural cost advantage in producing low-emissions hydrogen, particularly in comparison to electrolysers, as a key driver of customer interest. This cost advantage is critical in competitive evaluations where customers assess hydrogen production technologies based on delivered cost per kilogram, particularly for large-scale industrial applications.

The dual-product model creates additional value relative to single-product hydrogen technologies. The graphite co-product provides incremental revenue and improves overall project economics. As industrial customers and energy companies accelerate decarbonisation initiatives to meet regulatory requirements and corporate sustainability targets, demand for cost-competitive, scalable hydrogen production technologies is expected to grow. Hazer's deepening strategic partnership with KBR provides credibility and global reach in marketing these technologies to multinational industrial customers and energy companies pursuing decarbonisation investments.

title: Lufthansa stock trades steadily as traffic recovery and cost discipline shape investor focus
description:

Infrastructure constraints at key hub airports, such as Frankfurt and Munich, have at times influenced Lufthansa’s capacity decisions.
The effectiveness of these strategies is reflected in the variability of fuel costs from year to year and their share of overall operating expenses.

text:
Lufthansa stock sits at the intersection of Europe’s recovering air travel demand and the airline group’s ongoing restructuring efforts. The company, formally Deutsche Lufthansa AG (ISIN DE0008232125), remains a key constituent of the European airline sector, with its shares primarily traded on Xetra in euros. Investors continue to monitor the balance between passenger volume growth, yield development, and cost discipline as Lufthansa digests its post-crisis restructuring and pursues fleet renewal.

Revenue up strongly from crisis levels

In its latest available annual reporting for fiscal 2023, Deutsche Lufthansa AG reported group revenue running clearly above the crisis trough of 2020. The company disclosed multi-billion-euro revenue as air travel demand normalised across Europe and long-haul markets. Compared with the sharp downturn seen in 2020, when travel restrictions severely curtailed passenger numbers and cargo capacity, revenue increased significantly over subsequent years, reflecting both higher load factors and improved pricing in important markets. This revenue recovery, combined with tight control of operating costs, has allowed Lufthansa to return to positive operating profit and to generate positive cash flow from operations in recent reporting periods.

The revenue growth has been driven by several components. Passenger revenue benefitted from capacity ramp-up on European and transatlantic routes, while Lufthansa’s cargo operations took advantage of strong freight rates and robust demand for air freight capacity in key global trade corridors. As the company’s network carriers and point-to-point operations restored capacity, average yields recovered from depressed crisis levels. This contributed to year-on-year increases in revenue per available seat kilometer compared with 2020 and 2021, providing a crucial support for earnings. At the same time, the group has been gradually winding down government stabilization measures that were put in place during the pandemic, moving back toward a more normal balance-sheet structure.

Operating profit margin tied to cost base

Beyond top-line development, Lufthansa’s profitability has depended heavily on its unit cost trajectory. In recent reporting, the group has highlighted initiatives to improve efficiency across fleet operations, maintenance, and overhead functions. Measures such as fleet modernization, including the introduction of newer, more fuel-efficient aircraft, are intended to reduce fuel and maintenance costs per seat. In parallel, restructuring programs in administrative and ground operations have aimed to lower personnel and overhead expenses while preserving operational resilience during peak travel seasons.

Investors pay particular attention to Lufthansa’s operating margin and EBIT trajectory in comparison with other European network carriers. When revenue moved off the crisis trough, the group’s reported EBIT swung back toward positive territory after posting heavy losses in 2020. The EBIT improvement, combined with positive operating cash flow, has allowed Lufthansa to reduce net debt from its post-crisis peak. This deleveraging effort is supported by disciplined capital allocation, with fleet investments calibrated to expected demand and profitability. The group’s ability to maintain an acceptable leverage profile while funding necessary aircraft and infrastructure investments remains a central question for equity investors.

Passenger volumes and capacity trends

Passenger demand trends underpin the investment narrative around Lufthansa stock. As travel restrictions eased after 2020, the group reported steady increases in carried passengers, measured in millions per year across its network carriers, point-to-point brands and regional affiliates. Capacity, expressed in available seat kilometers, has been adjusted to match demand while avoiding overcapacity that could pressure yields. Seasonal peaks around major holiday periods have tested the resilience of Lufthansa’s operations, including ground handling, crew availability and maintenance scheduling.

Infrastructure constraints at key hub airports, such as Frankfurt and Munich, have at times influenced Lufthansa’s capacity decisions. Slot availability, ground service bottlenecks and air traffic control limitations can restrict the pace of capacity expansion even when demand is strong. Conversely, softer periods in business travel and long-haul leisure segments have prompted capacity trimming and schedule adjustments to protect yields. For investors, the interplay between capacity discipline and demand momentum translates directly into revenue per seat and ultimately into profit margins.

Balance sheet, liquidity and funding

Lufthansa’s balance sheet emerged from the crisis with elevated debt after the company tapped state-backed stabilization instruments and market funding to bridge the collapse in travel demand. Subsequent years of revenue recovery and positive operating cash flow have allowed the group to pay down parts of its debt stack and to refinance certain instruments on more favorable terms. Equity investors monitor metrics such as net debt to EBITDA and interest coverage to assess the sustainability of the capital structure.

Liquidity buffers, including cash and undrawn credit facilities, play a crucial role in the risk assessment of Lufthansa stock. The airline industry’s exposure to external shocks, ranging from geopolitical tensions to fuel price spikes and health-related travel advisories, demands robust liquidity management. Lufthansa has emphasized maintaining sufficient liquidity to weather demand setbacks while continuing to invest in fleet and product improvements. The balance between de-leveraging, dividend potential and growth investments remains a central topic in shareholder discussions.

Cost inflation and labor dynamics

Cost inflation and labor relations represent important risk factors. Rising fuel prices, airport and air traffic fees, and general inflation in maintenance and catering services can squeeze margins if not offset by higher yields or efficiency gains. In addition, wage negotiations with pilots, cabin crew and ground staff can lead to higher personnel costs and, in certain cases, to industrial action that affects operations. Lufthansa’s management aims to strike agreements that ensure operational stability while keeping unit costs competitive relative to European peers.

Investors consider the potential impact of labor disputes on revenue and costs, especially during peak travel seasons when disruptions can translate into significant compensation expenses and reputational damage. At the same time, attractive working conditions and career prospects are necessary to recruit and retain skilled personnel in a tight labor market for aviation professionals. Balancing these factors is a continuous task for Lufthansa’s leadership and has direct implications for shareholder value.

Fuel, hedging and environmental commitments

Fuel costs are another key line item in Lufthansa’s income statement. The group’s fuel expenditure depends on global oil prices, refining margins and currency movements, as jet fuel is typically priced in US dollars. Lufthansa uses hedging strategies to smooth the impact of fuel price volatility on its earnings. However, hedging can also lead to opportunity costs or additional expenses when market prices move unexpectedly. The effectiveness of these strategies is reflected in the variability of fuel costs from year to year and their share of overall operating expenses.

Environmental commitments and regulatory initiatives, including European emissions trading and sustainability-linked policies, shape Lufthansa’s long-term cost structure and investment needs. Fleet renewal with more efficient aircraft reduces per-seat emissions and fuel consumption but requires substantial capital spending. Additionally, efforts to support sustainable aviation fuel and other decarbonization technologies may involve partnerships and investments that affect cash flow. Equity investors increasingly incorporate these factors into their valuation frameworks, considering both potential regulatory costs and reputational benefits.

Competitive positioning relative to peers

Lufthansa operates in a competitive landscape featuring other European network carriers and low-cost airlines. The company’s multi-brand strategy, with full-service hub carriers and point-to-point brands, seeks to address business and leisure segments across short-haul and long-haul markets. Competitive dynamics influence pricing power, route profitability and load factors. On some routes, particularly within Europe, low-cost competitors exert downward pressure on fares, prompting Lufthansa to adjust capacity, pricing and service levels.

Internationally, competition from global network carriers affects Lufthansa’s share of premium traffic and cargo flows. The group’s membership in an alliance and its joint ventures on key intercontinental routes are designed to strengthen its competitive position and broaden its network reach. Investors assess whether Lufthansa’s network and partnerships translate into sustainable advantages in revenue and cost terms or whether competitive pressures risk eroding margins over time.

Dividend, capital allocation and shareholder returns

Capital allocation decisions, including dividend policy, are central to how Lufthansa stock is perceived by the market. After the crisis period, dividend resumption and future payout levels depend on the company’s earnings recovery, balance-sheet strength and investment needs. Management must weigh shareholder expectations for distributions against requirements for fleet investments, debt reduction and potential strategic initiatives.

Shareholder returns, measured through a combination of dividends and share price development, reflect market confidence in Lufthansa’s ability to generate sustainable cash flow and navigate industry cycles. If earnings normalize and leverage falls toward more conservative levels, the scope for more consistent dividend payments may expand. Conversely, unexpected shocks, elevated fuel costs or prolonged labor disputes could constrain distributable cash and lead to more cautious capital-return policies.

Product focus: long-haul passenger services

One representative product line for Lufthansa is its long-haul passenger services connecting Europe with North America, Asia and other regions. These routes typically offer multiple cabin classes, including economy, premium economy, business and, in some cases, first class. Product enhancements, such as upgraded seats, improved in-flight entertainment and connectivity, and refined catering options, aim to attract high-yield passengers and differentiate Lufthansa’s offerings from competitors.

Demand for long-haul travel is influenced by macroeconomic conditions, corporate travel budgets and tourism trends. Premium cabins, in particular, can contribute disproportionately to route profitability due to higher yields. Investments in cabin refurbishments, lounge infrastructure and digital booking tools are intended to support revenue per passenger and strengthen brand loyalty. For equity investors, the performance of these long-haul services is a key barometer of Lufthansa’s ability to capture value from global travel flows.

Stock price and market value context

In the context of European equity markets, Lufthansa stock trades as a cyclical airline share whose valuation typically reflects expectations about future traffic, yields and cost evolution rather than current earnings alone. The share price, quoted in euros on Xetra, responds strongly to changes in macroeconomic outlook, sector news such as fuel price trends, and company-specific developments including earnings releases and guidance updates. Market capitalization moves accordingly, signaling how investors collectively assess the group’s future cash generation potential.

For portfolio managers and retail investors, Lufthansa stock often serves as a levered play on European and global air travel demand. The share’s sensitivity to economic cycles, consumer confidence and business travel trends makes it a candidate for sector rotation strategies. At the same time, its exposure to operational risks and regulatory developments requires careful risk management. As the airline industry continues to adapt to structural changes and sustainability requirements, Lufthansa’s execution on its strategic priorities will remain central to how its shares are valued in the market.

Synopsis: Expansion across power generation, rail infrastructure, and shipbuilding is driving long-term growth for select public sector enterprises. Backed by large project pipelines and capacity additions, these companies are strengthening their position in India’s infrastructure and industrial development.

Capacity expansion and large-scale project execution are key drivers of long-term growth, enabling companies to increase revenues, improve operational efficiency, and strengthen their competitive position. Investments in new facilities and strategic projects also help create additional growth opportunities over time.

Backed by strong government support and rising infrastructure spending, several public sector enterprises are undertaking ambitious expansion plans across their core businesses. These initiatives are expected to enhance execution capabilities, diversify operations, and support sustainable earnings growth in the coming years.

NTPC Ltd

NTPC Ltd is one of the India’s largest power generation companies and a leading public sector enterprise engaged in the generation and sale of electricity. While thermal power remains its core business, the company is rapidly expanding its renewable energy portfolio, including solar, wind, green hydrogen, and battery energy storage systems (BESS). With a market capitalisation of Rs. 3,31,432 cr, the shares of NTPC Ltd closed at Rs. 341.80 per share, down from its previous close of Rs. 342.50 per share.

Capacity Under construction

As of 31 March 2026, NTPC Group had a total of 34,188 MW of power generation capacity under construction. This includes 16,520 MW of coal-based projects, 2,631 MW of hydro projects (including pumped storage), and 15,037 MW of renewable energy projects, reflecting the company’s diversified capacity expansion strategy.

The renewable energy pipeline forms a significant part of the expansion, with 14,479 MW under the NGEL Group and 15,037 MW for the overall NTPC Group. Key ongoing projects include 7,183 MW of solar and 4,165 MW of wind under NREL, along with multiple solar and wind projects through joint ventures, highlighting NTPC’s increasing focus on clean energy alongside conventional power generation.

It plans to add around 8 GW of renewable energy capacity, while also expanding into emerging clean energy segments. The company has commenced work at its Pudimadaka Green Hydrogen Hub to develop green methanol and sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), alongside advancing coal gasification projects aimed at enhancing the utilisation of domestic coal resources and diversifying its long-term energy portfolio.

Rail Vikas Nigam Ltd (RVNL)

Rail Vikas Nigam Ltd (RVNL) is a public sector enterprise under the Ministry of Railways responsible for implementing and executing rail infrastructure projects across India. Its portfolio includes new railway lines, track doubling, electrification, metro rail, bridges, stations, and other transportation infrastructure. With a market capitalisation of Rs. 47,006 cr, the shares of Rail Vikas Nigam Ltd closed at Rs. 225.45 per share, down from its previous close of Rs. 226.45 per share.

RVNL is executing the Rs. 13,236 crore BharatNet project awarded by BSNL to provide high-speed broadband connectivity in rural and remote areas through 8,206 km of optical fibre cable (OFC). The project has achieved 15.01% physical progress, with execution gaining momentum, and the company expects healthy revenue and profit margins from it during the current year.

Rishikesh–Karnaprayag Rail Project

The Rs. 37,000 crore Rishikesh–Karnaprayag Rail project has reached 74% overall completion, with nearly 96% of tunnel excavation completed. Targeted for completion by December 2029, the 125-km rail line is expected to significantly improve connectivity to the Himalayan region in Uttarakhand.

Vande Bharat Sleeper Train Project

RVNL, through its SPV Kinet Railway Solutions, is executing the Rs. 14,400 crore Vande Bharat sleeper train project, which includes a 35-year maintenance contract. The first prototype train is expected to be launched by December 2026, and the project has already received the Bronze A’ Design Award 2026 in Italy for excellence in mobility and transportation design.

Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Ltd (GRSE)

Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Ltd (GRSE) is a leading defence public sector undertaking engaged in the design and construction of warships, patrol vessels, survey ships, and other specialized vessels for the Indian Navy and Coast Guard.

With a market capitalisation of Rs. 29,563 cr, the shares of Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Ltd closed at Rs. 2580.75 per share, down from its previous close of Rs. 2,592.70 per share.

Capacity Expansion Plans

The company is expanding its shipbuilding capacity from 28 platforms to 32 platforms by the end of the current calendar year through ongoing modernization projects. In addition, it is setting up two brownfield shipbuilding facilities in West Bengal and two greenfield facilities, one each in West Bengal and Gujarat, to further strengthen its manufacturing capabilities.

The expansion is driven by the government’s Rs. 69,725 crore shipbuilding revitalization package and the growing pipeline of commercial shipbuilding demand identified by the Ministry of Shipping. The company expects these initiatives to accelerate growth in the commercial shipbuilding segment while enhancing its long-term production capacity.

text:
The International Air Transport Association (IATA) has criticized a European Commission proposal to extend the EU Emissions Trading Scheme (EU ETS) beyond Europe’s borders, calling the move a repeat of a mistake made more than a decade ago.

The global airline body said the plan would create friction over extraterritoriality, slow global efforts to cut aviation emissions, and weaken European competitiveness, with travelers and businesses in Europe ultimately bearing the cost.

“The EU is repeating a historic error. The consequences will be harmful, sowing acrimony over extraterritoriality, slowing global decarbonization, and sapping European competitiveness, with European travelers and businesses paying the price,” said Willie Walsh, IATA’s Director General.

The EU ETS is a carbon pricing system that requires airlines to buy allowances covering their emissions on flights within Europe. IATA’s statement, issued on 17 July 2026, refers to a similar attempt by the EU to apply the scheme to flights entering and leaving the bloc in 2012, a move that was suspended after it triggered a diplomatic backlash from countries including the United States, China and India.

IATA argues that instead of widening the EU ETS, the European Commission should strengthen the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA), the global carbon offset mechanism agreed through the International Civil Aviation Organization. IATA describes CORSIA as the agreed global mechanism for tackling aviation emissions and says the EU should focus its efforts on making that system more effective rather than pursuing a regional scheme with international reach.

The association points to two measures it says could support that goal: increasing the availability of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) allowances and introducing a book and claim system for SAF. Under a book and claim model, airlines could purchase the environmental benefits of sustainable fuel without needing to physically uplift it at every airport, a system aviation groups have said could accelerate SAF adoption where production and distribution are limited.

IATA cautioned that the details of any such measures would be critical to their success, without specifying what changes it is seeking from Brussels.

The association said it intends to engage directly with European policymakers to push for what it calls a more effective approach, one that avoids extraterritorial reach, fully supports CORSIA, and includes effective incentives for sustainable aviation fuel.

Aviation’s contribution to climate change has remained a central point of tension between airlines, regulators and environmental groups. Airlines have argued that a fragmented patchwork of regional and international carbon pricing schemes raises costs and creates legal uncertainty, while EU policymakers have said broader carbon pricing coverage is needed to meet the bloc’s climate targets.

IATA represents around 340 airlines worldwide and has repeatedly called for a single, globally coordinated approach to aviation emissions rather than overlapping regional rules. The organization’s latest statement signals that the debate over how far the EU’s carbon rules should extend is likely to continue as the European Commission moves forward with its proposed revision of the EU ETS.
