Berkaca dari kondisi tersebut, TP PKK Jawa Tengah menggandeng PT BioSirkular Inovasi Indonesia dan PT GML, untuk mengembangkan program pengelolaan minyak jelantah berbasis masyarakat.

Nawal menekankan, pengelolaan minyak jelantah menjadi sumber daya bernilai ekonomi membutuhkan kolaborasi multipihak, terutama keterlibatan keluarga sebagai aktor utama.

"Keberhasilan pengelolaan limbah minyak jelantah ini sangat bergantung sekali pada kesadaran dan partisipasi keluarga, terutama para ibu sebagai pengelola rumah tangga," tegasnya.

Melalui program ini, kader PKK di setiap desa dan kelurahan akan menjadi ujung tombak edukasi, sekaligus koordinator pengumpulan minyak jelantah. Gerakan ini nantinya juga diperluas melalui jaringan Posyandu yang jumlahnya mencapai 49.149 lembaga di Jawa Tengah.

"Bukan hanya PKK, nanti kita juga melibatkan Posyandu yang jumlahnya 49.149 lembaga. Ini merupakan potensi yang luar biasa untuk kita bisa membentuk ekonomi sirkular di Jawa Tengah," beber Nawal.

Menurutnya, konsep ekonomi sirkular menjadi sangat relevan, karena minyak jelantah tidak lagi dipandang sebagai limbah yang harus dibuang, melainkan sumber daya yang dapat dimanfaatkan kembali menjadi berbagai produk bernilai ekonomi.

"Bagaimana minyak jelantah ini juga menjadi sumber untuk diolah menjadi biodiesel misalnya, atau bioaftur maupun berbagai produk bernilai ekonomi lainnya," ungkap Ketua TP Posyandu Jateng tersebut.

Nawal menambahkan, saat ini minyak jelantah juga telah dimanfaatkan sebagai bahan baku pengembangan Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) di Kilang Pertamina Cilacap.

Pada kesempatan itu, pihaknya mengapresiasi TP PKK Kabupaten Batang yang lebih dahulu menerapkan program serupa. Dalam kurun waktu sekitar satu tahun sejak Juni 2025, program pengelolaan minyak jelantah di Batang mampu menghasilkan omzet hingga Rp170 juta.

"Ini membuktikan bahwa limbah rumah tangga kini telah menjadi bagian dari transisi, menuju energi yang lebih bersih dan berkelanjutan," imbuh istri Wakil Gubernur Jateng tersebut.

Sementara itu, Direktur PT BioSirkular Inovasi Indonesia Dicka Dwi Candra mengatakan, program tersebut merupakan tindak lanjut dari penandatanganan nota kesepahaman bersama TP PKK dan TP Posyandu Jateng, pada peringatan Hari Bumi, 22 April 2026 lalu.

Menurut Dicka, program dijalankan melalui empat aktivitas utama. Yakni edukasi masyarakat, penyediaan titik pengumpulan minyak jelantah di desa dan kelurahan, penjemputan oleh operator di tingkat kecamatan, serta pencatatan digital dan konversi hasil penjualan ke rekening masing-masing pengelola.

Dia menjelaskan, setiap satu liter minyak jelantah dihargai Rp7.000. Dari nilai tersebut, Rp5.000 diberikan kepada warga, sedangkan Rp2.000 masuk ke kas PKK desa. Proses konversi dilakukan melalui sistem digital, yang memungkinkan hasil penjualan dipantau secara transparan melalui aplikasi.

Selain memberikan tambahan penghasilan bagi masyarakat, program ini juga diharapkan mampu memperkuat peran kader PKK dan Posyandu, mendukung program lingkungan pemerintah daerah, serta menciptakan model pengelolaan limbah rumah tangga yang terukur dan berkelanjutan.

"Melalui program ini kita harap ekonomi sirkular berbasis rumah tangga akan aktif kembali dan menjadi penggerak untuk pembangunan keberlanjutan," kata Dicka.

Dalam kegiatan tersebut, TP PKK Jateng juga melakukan penandatanganan nota kesepakatan dengan PT Pegadaian (Persero) Kanwil XI Semarang, terkait sinergi program peningkatan pemberdayaan dan kesejahteraan keluarga, melalui gerakan pilah sampah menjadi tabungan emas. (*)

title: New 787 destined for Lufthansa to serve as ecoDemonstrator - Runway Girl
description:
A new Boeing 787 Dreamliner that is slated to be delivered to Lufthansa will first serve as Boeing’s newest ecoDemonstrator to flight test innovations that could improve fuel efficiency and reduce noise emissions.
These new procedures aim to curtail community noise around airports and identify opportunities for improving fuel efficiency.
First established in 2012, the ecoDemonstrator program advances the exploration of technologies that can help make aviation more efficient and sustainable.
In 2023, for example, sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) used in the ecoDemonstrator flight-test program was found to produce “dramatically” reduced soot particles and contrails.
We are pleased to support this year’s Boeing ecoDemonstrator Explorer program alongside Rolls-Royce,” says Lufthansa Group chief technology officer Grazia Vittadini of the carrier’s latest collaboration with Boeing.
text:
A new Boeing 787 Dreamliner that is slated to be delivered to Lufthansa will first serve as Boeing’s newest ecoDemonstrator to flight test innovations that could improve fuel efficiency and reduce noise emissions.

Powered by Rolls-Royce Trent 1000 engines, the 787-9 this month will begin testing a new reduced-length engine inlet with advanced acoustic treatments, in addition to new departure and arrival procedures.

The next-generation inlet “enables the integration of more fuel-efficient engines onto future platforms, and reduces weight and drag while maintaining the acoustic performance,” Boeing explains. Rolls-Royce provided engineering support and oversight for operating the modified Trent 1000 with the new inlet installed.

Also being explored are ‘Intelligent Operations’ flight paths, which are algorithmically generated using multiple data sources. These new procedures aim to curtail community noise around airports and identify opportunities for improving fuel efficiency.

The technologies being tested are part of Phase III of the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration’s CLEEN (Continuous Lower Energy, Emissions and Noise) program, a public-private partnership that sees government and aviation companies split the cost of researching and developing new green wing solutions.

First established in 2012, the ecoDemonstrator program advances the exploration of technologies that can help make aviation more efficient and sustainable. Through the years, Boeing has partnered with various airlines, including but not limited to Alaska Airlines, Etihad Airways, FedEx and United Airlines, and has evaluated more than 260 technologies, including more sustainable cabin interiors.

Their work has been quite meaningful. In 2023, for example, sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) used in the ecoDemonstrator flight-test program was found to produce “dramatically” reduced soot particles and contrails.

“Lufthansa Group and Boeing share a long-standing partnership in aviation. We are pleased to support this year’s Boeing ecoDemonstrator Explorer program alongside Rolls-Royce,” says Lufthansa Group chief technology officer Grazia Vittadini of the carrier’s latest collaboration with Boeing.

“Together, we aim to help advance aviation’s transformation by testing technologies with the potential to improve fuel efficiency, reduce noise and prove their value in real-world operations. ”

Testing begins later this month at the Boeing site in Glasgow, Montana, and is expected to run through mid-August.

title: United Airlines stock edges higher as higher fares and loyalty revenue support margins
description:

text:
United Airlines stock sits at the intersection of robust travel demand and a complex cost backdrop as the carrier prepares for its next set of quarterly results. The Chicago based airline group United Airlines Holdings Inc. (ISIN US9100471096) has reported rising passenger revenue and growing loyalty program income over recent quarters, while investors watch closely how higher fares and premium offerings translate into sustainable margins in an environment of volatile fuel prices and ongoing labor cost pressure.

Revenue climbs with strong passenger demand

In its recent financial reporting, United Airlines has highlighted that total operating revenue increased compared with the prior year period, driven primarily by higher passenger revenue and additional income from its MileagePlus loyalty program. For example, in a recent quarter United disclosed that total revenue reached a level clearly above the same quarter a year earlier, supported by a double digit increase in passenger revenue and a notable contribution from other operating income such as credit card partnerships and ancillary fees. This improvement reflects continued recovery in international travel and sustained domestic demand, particularly on transatlantic and transpacific routes where yields have been higher than pre pandemic benchmarks.

The airline also noted that unit revenue metrics such as revenue per available seat mile rose versus the prior year, indicating that the company has been able to charge higher average fares or secure stronger mix toward premium cabins and preferred seating. In addition, corporate and high yield business travel has gradually returned, contributing to year over year gains in premium revenue. United’s management has emphasized that these dynamics, together with capacity discipline and a focus on profitable routes, have been central in driving revenue growth and improving the top line compared with the previous year.

Operating income improves against prior year

Alongside higher revenue, United Airlines has reported improved operating income relative to the same period in the prior year, even after accounting for elevated fuel and labor expenses. Operating margin expanded versus the comparable quarter, reflecting a combination of stronger yields, better load factors, and ongoing cost initiatives. In a recent quarter the company indicated that operating income rose by a meaningful amount year on year, and that adjusted operating margin came in above the level it had achieved in the equivalent quarter before. This was facilitated by higher capacity utilization, with available seat miles growing while maintaining or enhancing revenue per seat, and by optimization of its route network to focus on markets with stronger profitability.

Management has also pointed to nonfuel cost control as a factor in the improved operating performance. While salaries and wages have increased following new labor agreements and the need to retain and train staff, the airline has worked to offset these pressures through efficiency measures, better scheduling, and technology investments. As a result, the growth in nonfuel unit costs has been kept in check relative to revenue growth, supporting the expansion in operating income compared to the prior year period.

Earnings rebound compared with last year

United Airlines has reported that net income and earnings per share rebounded compared with the prior year quarter, moving from a lower profit base toward more normalized levels as demand recovered and international routes reopened more fully. In a recent quarter the carrier stated that diluted earnings per share were clearly ahead of the figure reported in the same quarter a year earlier, with adjusted earnings metrics similarly showing improvement versus prior year comparisons. This recovery in earnings has been attributed to the combination of higher revenue, improved load factors, and better pricing, together with the benefits of loyalty and co branded credit card revenue, which typically carries strong margins.

The company has emphasized that international long haul operations, especially transatlantic flights connecting the United States with major European hubs and transpacific services to Asia, have been key contributors to this earnings improvement. These routes often generate higher average fares and premium cabin utilization, which in turn help lift overall profitability relative to domestic operations. Management has indicated that demand in these markets is running above prior year levels, and in some cases above pre pandemic benchmarks, supporting a year over year increase in earnings.

Guidance signals cautious optimism

Looking ahead, United Airlines has provided guidance that suggests cautious optimism, with expectations for continued revenue growth and stable to improving margins, assuming demand remains resilient and fuel prices do not spike significantly. The company has indicated that it expects total revenue in upcoming quarters to be above the comparable prior year periods, driven by capacity growth in international markets and ongoing strength in premium and loyalty revenue. At the same time, United has acknowledged that cost inflation, particularly in labor and maintenance, as well as potential volatility in jet fuel prices, could weigh on margins, and has thus framed its outlook in measured terms.

United’s guidance typically includes projections for key metrics such as capacity growth in available seat miles, revenue per available seat mile trends, and adjusted operating margin ranges. These indicators provide investors with a quantified view of how the airline expects to balance growth and profitability. In recent guidance, the company has signaled that capacity will grow versus the prior year quarter, while unit revenue and margin are intended to remain at or slightly above the levels achieved previously, reflecting management’s strategy of focusing on profitable growth rather than simply chasing volume.

Balance sheet and debt profile

The financial position of United Airlines remains a central consideration for investors, given the capital intensive nature of the airline industry and the debt taken on during the pandemic period. United has reported total debt at levels higher than before the crisis, but it has also highlighted progress in reducing net debt through improved cash flow and selective debt repayment. In its recent filings the company has described a reduction in net debt compared with the prior year, supported by stronger operating cash flow and cautious capital expenditure planning. This trend is important for equity holders because lower leverage can reduce interest expense and financial risk over time.

United’s cash and liquidity position has continued to be robust, with available liquidity including cash, short term investments, and undrawn credit facilities comfortably exceeding near term obligations. The airline has emphasized that maintaining strong liquidity is a strategic priority, as it allows the company to manage periods of demand volatility, fund fleet investments, and service debt without undue strain. Over recent quarters, operating cash flow has been positive and improved relative to the prior year period, in line with higher earnings and better working capital management.

Fleet investments and capital expenditure

United Airlines is in the midst of a significant fleet modernization and expansion program, which has implications for both its cost structure and customer experience. The company has placed substantial aircraft orders with major manufacturers, including new narrowbody and widebody aircraft designed to improve fuel efficiency and offer enhanced cabin amenities. These investments, while capital intensive, are aimed at reducing unit fuel costs, improving reliability, and enabling growth in core markets such as long haul international and high density domestic routes.

Recent financial disclosures from United have indicated that capital expenditures have increased compared with the prior year, reflecting ongoing aircraft deliveries, retrofits, and investments in airport infrastructure and technology. Management has stated that these investments are expected to yield benefits over the medium term in the form of lower maintenance costs, improved fuel efficiency, and higher revenue potential from upgraded cabins and better on board connectivity. For investors, the pace and scale of capital expenditure relative to cash flow and debt reduction are key factors in assessing the long term risk and reward profile of United Airlines stock.

Fuel costs and hedging strategy

Jet fuel expense is one of the largest variable costs for United Airlines, and movements in crude oil prices can have a direct and significant impact on the company’s profitability. In recent quarters United has reported higher fuel costs compared with the prior year, as average fuel prices per gallon have risen from earlier levels. The airline has responded through fare adjustments, capacity planning, and operational measures to improve fuel efficiency, such as deploying newer aircraft and optimizing flight paths and speeds. These steps help mitigate the impact of fuel price volatility on margins, but they cannot fully eliminate the underlying cost pressure.

United’s hedging strategy has historically been more limited than some peers, with the company often preferring to manage fuel exposure through its broader commercial and operational strategy rather than extensive derivative hedging. As a result, United’s reported fuel expense tends to track relatively closely with market prices, making its earnings sensitive to swings in energy markets. Investors therefore pay close attention to management commentary on fuel price assumptions in guidance and its plans to offset potential increases through revenue management and cost initiatives.

Labor costs and workforce dynamics

Labor is another major cost component for United Airlines, encompassing pilots, cabin crew, ground staff, maintenance personnel, and administrative employees. In recent periods, United has negotiated new labor agreements reflecting higher wages and benefits, which have increased overall labor expense compared with the prior year. The company has indicated that these agreements are essential to retaining skilled staff, ensuring operational reliability, and meeting regulatory and safety requirements, even though they contribute to nonfuel cost inflation.

At the same time, United has worked to improve productivity and efficiency through scheduling optimization, training programs, and technology that supports workforce management. For example, enhanced crew management systems and predictive maintenance tools can reduce delays and cancellations, thereby limiting the need for costly overtime and disruption related expenses. The balance between fair compensation and efficiency gains is critical for sustaining margins, and United’s ability to manage this balance influences how investors view United Airlines stock.

MileagePlus and loyalty revenue growth

One of the most attractive assets within United Airlines’ business model is its MileagePlus loyalty program, which generates significant revenue through partnerships with credit card issuers, retailers, and other travel providers. In recent quarters, United has reported that loyalty and co branded credit card revenue has grown compared with the prior year period, contributing to a higher share of total revenue. This income is typically less cyclical than ticket sales and carries strong margins, providing a stabilizing effect on the company’s overall earnings profile.

The growth in MileagePlus revenue underscores the value of United’s customer base and its ability to monetize travel spending beyond the flight itself. As more customers enroll in the program and use co branded cards, United benefits from fees and revenue sharing arrangements that can rise steadily over time. For investors, the expansion of loyalty revenue is a key component of the investment case for United Airlines stock, as it diversifies the company’s income streams and supports margin resilience in periods when demand or pricing for core air travel may moderate.

Comparison with peers and industry context

When comparing United Airlines with other large US carriers, investors often look at metrics such as revenue growth, margin performance, leverage, and network strength. Recent industry data suggest that United’s revenue growth and margin recovery have been broadly comparable with peers, though differences in network focus and capital allocation strategies can lead to variations in performance. United’s strong presence in major hubs such as Chicago, Newark, and San Francisco, combined with extensive international routes, gives it a distinct profile compared with carriers that are more concentrated in domestic or regional markets.

United’s leverage remains higher than some competitors due to the debt taken on during the pandemic and the scale of its fleet investment program, which may be seen as a risk factor by more conservative investors. However, its improving cash flow and focus on debt reduction over time mitigate this concern to some extent. The airline industry as a whole continues to face challenges such as regulatory requirements, environmental pressures, and exposure to economic cycles, and United is no exception. Nonetheless, the company’s revenue and earnings recovery relative to the prior year provide evidence that United Airlines has been able to navigate these challenges while maintaining a competitive position in the market.

Environmental strategy and sustainability initiatives

United Airlines has publicly committed to various environmental and sustainability goals, including reducing its greenhouse gas emissions and investing in sustainable aviation fuel and more efficient aircraft. These initiatives, while only partially reflected in current financial metrics, have long term implications for cost structure and regulatory risk. United’s investments in new aircraft, operational efficiency, and partnerships related to sustainable aviation fuel are intended to lower emissions per passenger and per flight over time, aligning the company with evolving regulatory standards and customer preferences.

From an investor perspective, these sustainability efforts are relevant for assessing future capital expenditure requirements, potential carbon related costs, and the airline’s ability to meet increasingly stringent environmental regulations. United’s progress in these areas can influence its reputation and customer loyalty, which in turn may affect revenue and profitability. Although the immediate financial impact of sustainability initiatives may be modest, the longer term benefits in terms of reduced risk and potential competitive advantage are a factor in how some investors evaluate United Airlines stock.

Risk factors and volatility considerations

Investing in airlines involves a range of risk factors, and United Airlines is subject to many of them. These include macroeconomic conditions that influence travel demand, geopolitical events affecting international routes, regulatory changes, labor relations, fuel price volatility, and operational disruptions such as weather or technical issues. United’s management acknowledges these risks in its disclosures and emphasizes the importance of maintaining strong liquidity, diversified revenue streams, and flexible capacity management to navigate periods of turbulence.

Historically, airline stocks have exhibited significant price volatility, and United Airlines stock is no exception. Earnings can fluctuate markedly from quarter to quarter as demand, pricing, and costs move, and market sentiment toward the sector can change quickly in response to external events. For this reason, investors often look beyond a single quarter’s figures and focus on trends over several periods, such as year over year revenue and earnings growth, margin stability, and progress in reducing debt. United’s recent trajectory of improving revenue and earnings compared with the prior year, together with its investment in fleet and loyalty assets, forms the basis for many assessments of its medium term prospects.

Product and service focus across cabins

United Airlines offers a range of products and services across cabin classes, including United Polaris business class on long haul international flights, premium economy offerings, economy plus seating with extra legroom, and standard economy. The airline has invested in upgrading cabins, improving seats, enhancing in flight entertainment, and expanding Wi Fi connectivity, particularly on routes that carry higher proportions of business and premium leisure travelers. These product enhancements are designed to support higher yields and improved customer satisfaction, which in turn can contribute to revenue growth and margin improvements.

In addition to on board products, United has focused on its digital platforms and customer service, including mobile apps and website functionality that facilitate booking, check in, and management of MileagePlus accounts. The carrier’s customer experience strategy aims to differentiate its offering in competitive markets and build loyalty among frequent travelers. For investors, the linkage between product quality, customer satisfaction scores, and financial performance is an important consideration, as better products can support higher fares and repeat business, thereby reinforcing the revenue trends that underpin United Airlines stock.

United Airlines stock and market valuation

United Airlines stock trades primarily on the Nasdaq exchange under the symbol UAL, and its market valuation reflects investor expectations regarding future revenue, earnings, and cash flow. As of a recent trading day, the shares were priced at a level that implies a market capitalization in the multiple billions of USD, positioning United among the larger constituents of major US equity indices that include airline stocks. The share price has moved over time in response to quarterly results, guidance updates, macroeconomic news, and sector specific developments such as changes in fuel prices or regulatory announcements.

Equity analysts and market participants often compare United’s valuation metrics, such as price to earnings and enterprise value to EBITDA, with those of peers to assess whether the stock trades at a premium or discount to the sector based on its growth and risk profile. United’s improved earnings and cash flow compared with the prior year can support a case for valuation normalization after the disruptions of the pandemic period. However, the inherent cyclicality and risk in the airline business mean that investors usually maintain a degree of caution, and United Airlines stock remains sensitive to shifts in risk appetite and sector sentiment.

text:
A north Queensland cattle farming family is taking part in a trial growing oil-producing trees alongside livestock.

The Lawrie family, from Powlathanga station near Charters Towers in north Queensland, has been running a cattle breeding operation since 2004.

But now the family is taking part in a new venture.

In September last year, they turned a 10-hectare paddock into a renewable fuel trial, planting the oil-producing pongamia trees.

The trial is being completed with SilvoPlus, an entity of renewable fuel company JetZero Australia.

They're trying to determine the best way to run livestock alongside rows of pongamia, a legume tree with seeds containing oil that can be processed into biofuel.

Powlathanga grazier, Stephen Lawrie, said they wanted to take part in the trial to look at diversifying their income.

"You're always looking at different options, if something else interesting comes up that can work in conjunction with the cattle, I'm definitely interested in it," he said.

Ketti Ketmontri, the project lead for SilvoPlus, said the main purpose was to test the trees with grazing.

"We're looking at optimised grazing, how to produce fodder or cash crops in the interrow, and then when's the right time to bring sheep or cattle in," Mr Ketmontri said.

Trials across the country, nowhere to process

Pongamia trials have been breaking ground across Australia over the past decade, but there is currently nowhere that processes the oil into biofuel.

Ed Mason, CEO of JetZero Australia, has plans to build a biorefinery in Townsville that would take agricultural products and process them into sustainable aviation fuel (SAF).

"We're looking to take bioethanol and take about a hundred million litres of sustainable aviation fuel as well as renewable diesel," he said.

"That's a material volume for Townsville, enough to supply most of the airports in the region if we were to do that."

Demand for SAF is growing, with 38 countries now having a mandate for airlines to use it.

JetZero has completed road construction and land clearing at a 150ha site in Townsville, with the company expected to reach financial close at the end of this year.

"It would be two years of construction and we're trying to accelerate that and compress that as much as we can with our engineering contractors," said Mr Mason.

"First fuels will hopefully be coming by 2028."

A potential cattle feed source

Scientists are looking at the nutritional value of the outside shell of pongamia seeds to be used as cattle feed.

Associate Professor from the University of Queensland Sarah Meale has just finished a study feeding ground-up pongamia husk to cattle.

"The pongamia husks are the byproduct of that oil extraction. So, it's a very cheap feed source that is really quite high in protein. So up to around 20 to 30 per cent protein."

The trial included a zero, two and four per cent inclusion rate of the ground pongamia.

"Across all treatments, we have seen the exact same intake and the same growth rates, which is a really promising outcome."

"Right now, we know cottonseed is hard to find and very, very expensive along with other protein sources. This is the potential to replace those at a much lower cost."

Although the experiment had promising results, the lack of pongamia oil processing is a roadblock for the feed to be used more widespread.

"The scale at the moment is the problem. We don't have enough of the product to make it into the market."

Cattle to be priority

On Powlathanga, Stephen Lawrie remains interested in the future of pongamia, but wants cattle to remain the focus.

"Unless the trees could produce twice the amount of income as what the cattle could, we couldn't really consider it," he said.

"But if they can be run in conjunction, I think it's a win-win."

A stay at Sterling Padam Pench highlights a growing preference among travellers for nature-led escapes that prioritise immersion over activity-heavy itineraries. Located close to Pench National Park, the property serves as a base for those looking to engage more closely with the forest landscape.

A Forest Stay at Sterling Padam Pench Redefines Wildlife Travel

Pench has long been associated with wildlife tourism, particularly for its tiger reserve, but the broader experience extends beyond sightings. The surrounding teak forests, early morning light filtering through dense canopies, and the constant presence of birds and smaller wildlife create an environment that rewards slower exploration. For photographers, especially, the shifting light and natural textures offer as much interest as the wildlife itself.

Sterling Padam Pench is positioned to support this pace. The property integrates into its surroundings without overpowering them, allowing the forest to remain central to the experience. Guests can return from safaris or walks to a space that feels relaxed and functional, without disconnecting from the environment they came to experience. The rhythm of the stay often mirrors the forest itself—early starts, quieter afternoons, and evenings that naturally slow down.

For those planning a wildlife-focused trip or a broader nature getaway in Madhya Pradesh, the property offers a combination of accessibility and immersion. It caters to photographers, nature enthusiasts, and travellers looking to step away from routine, even if only briefly.

Ultimately, a visit to Sterling Padam Pench is less about ticking off wildlife sightings and more about engaging with the forest as a whole. text:
Kinley Yangzom

Bhutan will serve as the primary research and certification hub for a pioneering international venture aimed at producing sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and biodegradable plastics from Pongamia trees.

The initiative, launched in Thimphu yesterday, establishes a strategic partnership between the Australian biotechnology company Ecopha and the Bhutanese company DrukBees Private Limited.

The project will focus on building a localised demonstration model in Bhutan before scaling the system up for larger global economies.

Speaking at the launch, Ecopha Chief Executive Officer and Co-founder Dr Wilson Ling said Bhutan’s renowned environmental leadership made it the ideal environment to prove the viability of a complete, replicable green system.

“We know that there is limited land and limited manpower in Bhutan, but we can make the whole system as a demonstration model and then show it to the world,” he said. “We show the result and the answer to everyone, and then countries like America, China, and India can follow accordingly.”

The core of the project relies on the cultivation of the Pongamia tree.

The non-edible seeds harvested from these trees produce an oil that can be processed directly into SAF, while the residual materials left over from refining will be utilised to manufacture biodegradable plastics.

Because Pongamia thrives on degraded land and does not compete with traditional food crops, the company considers the project a dual win for ecological restoration and renewable raw material production.

Rather than building a large industrial facility, the joint venture plans to start small by establishing precise Pongamia plantations and a localised biorefinery.

Nganglam has been identified as the preferred location for the initial plantation, with the first round of planting targeted for September.

Punakha is also currently being assessed for expansion following a recent site evaluation visit. The newly planted trees are expected to take approximately five years to mature before yielding seeds for processing.

To ensure strict compliance and product integrity, the company will deploy an advanced traceability system to digitally monitor every tree from planting to harvest. This system will record growth rates, geographic location, and environmental data, providing the foundational metrics needed to develop a global certification standard for all derived products.

Karma Dorji, promoter of Ecopha DrukBees Private Limited, said that Bhutan’s value in the partnership lies in intellectual and data-driven assets, rather than industrial volume.

“The mass production will happen in these big countries, but the model, certification, research and development, and the high-value work will happen in Bhutan because Bhutan is the right country to certify this product,” he said.

The company plans to spend the next five years maturing the complete research, tracking, and certification framework in Bhutan, establishing a blueprint that will eventually dictate the parameters for sustainable aviation products in much larger international markets.
